snippet.title: SciExplorer: From Microscopy Data to Interactive Scientific Visualisation — BCON26
snippet.description:
"SciExplorer: From Microscopy Data to Interactive Scientific Visualisation" by Alisa Ovsiannikova at Blender Conference 2026

Just as telescopes reveal the wonders of our cosmos, microscopes uncover the secrets of life. Biologists use modern microscopy to produce 3D imaging data from tissues, single cells, and even subcellular structures. However, understanding these data remains challenging.

Blender already supports importing and scientifically rendering microscopy data, yet interactive analysis is limited.

In this talk Alisa Ovsiannikova will introduce SciExplorer, a Python-based UI panel linking microscopy-derived data with measurements, allowing scientists to study biological structures interactively in 3D. For example, measured distances between structures become more intuitive when visualised in 3D, as they exist in real life, rather than as a list of numbers.

–

Learn more about Blender Conference 2026 at https://conference.blender.org/2026/

snippet.title: Scientific Data on Surfaces — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Scientific Data on Surfaces" by Nicole Feng at Blender Conference 2026

I'm a computer scientist working in "geometric computing", meaning I develop algorithms for working with geometric data like meshes, curves, and point clouds. In many projects, I've needed to accurately visualize data that lives on curved surfaces: Blender makes lighting, shading, and materials easy, but accurately communicating the behavior of a particular surface quantity, as it bends and wraps around 3D shapes, takes a little care. This talk is a short tour of basic techniques I've picked up for rendering surface quantities like scalar and vector fields, and also how I use Blender to help with scientific illustrations.

–

snippet.title: Designing Lattice Infills to Control Mechanical Behaviour — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Designing Lattice Infills to Control Mechanical Behaviour" by Mehmet Kala at Blender Conference 2026

Mehmet Kala will present his procedural lattice generation system that explores how geometry can do more than simply fill space. By controlling the arrangement and movement of lattice cells, the same material can be guided toward very different mechanical responses. Through physical prototypes, early testing, and concept applications such as personalized cushioning, artificial muscles, and morphing structures, the talk explores how lattice infill can evolve from a lightweight internal structure into an active part of a product’s mechanical behavior.

–

snippet.title: APX & AVX10: The Next Evolution of x86 — BCON26
snippet.description:
"APX & AVX10: The Next Evolution of x86" by Leonhard Rannabauer at Blender Conference 2026

The x86 CPU instruction set continues to evolve with new extensions that matter for performance-critical software like Blender. 
For developers, understanding these changes helps shape future optimizations to make better use of upcoming CPUs. 
In this talk, we introduce Advanced Performance Extensions (APX) and Advanced Vector Extensions 10 (AVX10), 
explain core ideas such as more general-purpose registers, cleaner instruction forms, 
and a more unified vector programming model.
We'll show what they enable in practice and where they bring measurable benefits in Blender.

–

snippet.description:
"Intel Open Image Denoise 3: Fast Temporal Denoising & Supersampling in Cycles" by Christoph Neuhauser at Blender Conference 2026

Intel Open Image Denoise (OIDN) is an open-source software library of high-performance, high-quality denoising filters for images rendered with ray tracing. The upcoming OIDN 3 release will feature a new network architecture enabling temporal denoising and supersampling up to 3x. For online rendering, this gives artists the ability to preview their scenes in Cycles faster and at a higher quality. For offline rendering, this will result in improved visual quality in general and in dynamic scenes in particular.

snippet.title: From Scene to Sensor: Synthetic LiDAR for Autonomous Systems — BCON26
snippet.description:
"From Scene to Sensor: Synthetic LiDAR for Autonomous Systems" by Michael Schwingshackl at Blender Conference 2026

Building high-quality LiDAR datasets for autonomous systems is slow, expensive, and rarely captures the edge cases that matter most. In this talk Michael Schwingshackl shows how a procedural pipeline turns synthetic 3D environments into physically accurate LiDAR scans. He walks through Geometry Nodes as a flexible sensor simulator, capable of reproducing complex real-world scan patterns, and Python for automated data extraction, turning Blender into a high-fidelity data engine for perception research. Michael presents results from outdoor autonomous machinery in the field and discusses how perception models trained on synthetic data perform once they leave simulation, including where the sim-to-real gap still causes trouble.

–

Throughout my career, I have explored and developed unconventional workflows to maintain greater control over the design process and improve project efficiency. For the past 15 years, Blender has been my primary tool for managing both the formal and technical aspects of projects across multiple disciplines, including interior design, product design, architecture, and urban planning. Working in these diverse fields exposed me to a wide range of challenges and led me to create custom workflows and tools that enhance productivity and support informed design decisions. The following examples showcase some of the most representative outcomes of this approach.

snippet.title: Fall of Reach - Guide to Epic Sci-Fi for Small Studios — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Fall of Reach - Guide to Epic Sci-Fi for Small Studios" by Julien Blarel at Blender Conference 2026

Can small teams succeed where Hollywood fails? 

Increasingly the answer is yes. But some projects still seem impossible, especially when it comes to capturing the epic scale of Halo's sci-fi universe. But we proved it could be done by producing an animated TV series on the Fall of Reach. (Note: THIS IS AN UNOFFICIAL FAN PROJECT)

This presentation uses our Blender project as a case study to show how a small team of independent creators can in fact deliver the massive scale, military realism, and complex lore that fans expect from major studios. From ideation and tooling to production pipelines and team structure, attendees will gain a practical roadmap for bringing ambitious stories to life.

"Cella: 3D Data Visualization for Plant Single-Cell Transcriptomics" by Sampo Muranen at Blender Conference 2026

Recent advancements in single-cell RNA sequencing have facilitated the possibility of acquiring vast amounts of data at single-cell resolution. This development has provided a broader and more comprehensive understanding of complex biological processes. The growing datasets require a visualization tool that transforms complex data into an intuitive representation. To address this challenge, we have utilized Blender to design Cella, a cell atlas visualization tool, which transforms data into 3D heatmaps that can be rendered into image libraries. Our tool is designed to support especially research on plant developmental biology.

snippet.title: Building Procedural Simulation Environments — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Building Procedural Simulation Environments" by Felipe Oliveira Ribas at Blender Conference 2026

Ray-tracing simulations are becoming faster and more accessible through modern graphics processing units and improved algorithms. However, the 3D environments used in these simulations are still often static, simplified, and manually prepared for a single scenario. This talk explores how Blender can become a procedural scene-generation layer for simulation. Geometry Nodes and Python can create controlled scene variations, expose geometric assumptions, and generate different levels of detail for different computational budgets. Electromagnetic propagation is presented as one practical example of this broader workflow.

snippet.title: PBRT 2: Creating and Working with Large Scenes — BCON26
snippet.description:
"PBRT 2: Creating and Working with Large Scenes" by Gustaf Waldemarson at Blender Conference 2026

Today, Blender is undeniably one of the best tools out there for a large swathe of graphics related tasks. However, some work can be done to make it even more useful when working with the complex scenes that are often used in graphics research.

During BCON24, I demonstrated how to create basic importers and exporters with the Python API using the PBRT format as a basis. In this talk, I will present various improvements to the importer that allows PBRT scenes to be rendered with Cycles at a comparable image quality, and by extension, leverage the existing Blender ecosystem to export these scenes to other systems via other formats, such as glTF.

Additionally, as some of these scenes contain numerous, or complex objects, techniques for working with them in a way that maintains user-interface responsiveness are highlighted.

I'll walk through the add-on's architecture:

2. Dynamic 3D-bounding-box masking 
3. Adaptive interpolation that respects "animating on ones, twos, and threes." 

By the end of the presentation, attendees will be able to replicate the approach themselves—and everyone who attends this presentation gets the add-on for free.

snippet.title: The Spinal Spline: Geometry Nodes Framework for Built Environments — BCON26
snippet.description:
"The Spinal Spline: Geometry Nodes Framework for Built Environments" by Gilad Harnik at Blender Conference 2026

Making architectural renders is more than just high quality assets and materials. It's about capturing the essence of the city and the environment. Analyzing different urban designs reveals that everything can be stripped down to a repetitive pattern. Essentially, it's a distribution problem.
In Blender this of course means: Array Along Curve. We will explore the "Even" and "Un-Even" methods to distribute objects on curve; why is it so important for the array to be "instance aware"; the research process; the implementation in Geometry Nodes; and finally some practical demos of our in-house workflow.

–

snippet.title: Yuify Your Mesh to Say Who Made It: Micromarking and Self-Sovereign Identity — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Yuify Your Mesh to Say Who Made It: Micromarking and Self-Sovereign Identity" by Lars Lenz, Joss Giffard-Burley at Blender Conference 2026

Digital work is easy to copy and hard to attribute. Wacom's Creative Rights Initiative exists to do something about the second half of that. The mission is to give creators a practical way to establish that a piece is theirs, and to demonstrate it later if it's ever in question. Yuify was the first result. Invisible Micromarks bind 2D image to a decentralized identifier and a signed authorship record, shipping today.

With 3D Micromarking Wacom is extending its Yuify service capabilities to 3D, where nothing sits still, with no canonical vertex ordering, no fixed sampling positions, and pipelines entitled to rewrite everything on export. Different data, different signals, different failure modes brought us a whole lot of interesting new problems.

In this session, you will learn what Yuify and 3D Micromarking is and how Wacom is trying to make authorship evidence survive a 3D pipeline.

–

Learn more about Blender Conference 2026 at https://conference.blender.org/2026/

snippet.title: Build Your Node Trees With Code — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Build Your Node Trees With Code" by Brady Johnston at Blender Conference 2026

In this talk Brady Johnston will present `nodebpy`, a new Python package for authoring, versioning and comparing node trees. Visual programming with nodes is excellent for iteration and artist-friendly workflows, but creating and tracking node trees in code has stayed verbose and difficult. With`nodebpy`, human-writeable code becomes nicely arranged node trees, and GUI-authored trees become human-readable `.py` files, making collaboration and review far easier. Shorter, more logical scripts also let LLMs read and write node trees more reliably and with less token usage. Brady will cover the  issues it solves, the design process behind the package, how it's currently used in several add-ons, and how you could start using it in pipelines and to version-control node trees.

–

snippet.title: Building KIDDO : Merging Polygonal Modeling, CAD, and Electronics — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Building KIDDO : Merging Polygonal Modeling, CAD, and Electronics" by Obride Deki at Blender Conference 2026

How do you turn a concept into an interactive action figure with 150+ parts, embedded electronics, custom voice lines, and LED effects?
Obride has the answers! 
This case study follows the full product lifecycle: from the creative phase in Blender (design, shape exploration, blockout), to the handoff to SolidWorks for precise engineering and integration of embedded electronics, and finally back to Blender to build a digital twin ready to be rendered and animated.

–

Learn more about Blender Conference 2026 at https://conference.blender.org/2026/

snippet.title: Grease Pencil Goodies - Story Tools, New Brushes & the VSE Editor — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Grease Pencil Goodies - Story Tools, New Brushes & the VSE Editor" by Laura Gingrich at Blender Conference 2026

This afternoon, we're exploring the exciting developments for storyboard and vis dev artists. This summer, the developers have released a new brush pack that includes a fantastic array of oils, charcoals, and foliage. We'll play with these tools for thumbnails and exploration, color keys and projection mapping. Then we'll look at implementing a 3D car into 2D environments, and we'll string it together with the new Storyboarding workflow.

–

snippet.title: Fisherwoman Item Song — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Fisherwoman Item Song" by Suresh Eriyat at Blender Conference 2026

At Studio Eeksaurus, we would like to showcase, that how an agile team could deliver stunning, industry standard visuals that compete with major productions. Featuring our upcoming short music video made in blender, Fisherwoman, this presentation showcases how we harnessed Blender’s accessible toolset and vast learning ecosystem to maximize our creative freedom. We will break down our stylized texturing and lighting workflows, demonstrating how a boutique studio can push artistic boundaries without a massive pipeline. It’s a testament to how the right tools empower small teams to create premium, world-class animation.

–

snippet.title: The Quest for the Ultimate Stylized Mouth Rig — BCON26
snippet.description:
"The Quest for the Ultimate Stylized Mouth Rig" by Maor Fridman at Blender Conference 2026

Ever since my student days, I’ve been obsessed with creating the ultimate, most versatile cartoon mouth rig—one that delivers highly flexible, appealing shapes. In our latest short film, "Finding Rozy," this journey culminated in a new approach: a Geometry Nodes-based system heavily inspired by Pixar’s Win or Lose. While it’s closer than ever to my dream rig, it still faces some technical bottlenecks. This talk explores that evolution, breaks down the setup, and invites the community to help troubleshoot and perfect the ultimate mouth workflow

–

snippet.title: Non-Destructive Mesh Fusion Without SDF or Remesh — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Non-Destructive Mesh Fusion Without SDF or Remesh" by Mattia Miccoli at Blender Conference 2026

Fusing one mesh smoothly into another has always been a pain. The usual routes are destructive edits, signed distance fields, or remeshing, and they all bake away the freedom to keep iterating. Mattia Miccoli built a fully non-destructive way to fuse geometry and materials that avoids SDF and remesh entirely, with every parameter adjustable in real time on top of the original topology. In this talk he shows how the approach works, where it helps most in modeling and hard-surface work, and what shipping a brand new kind of tool taught him.

–

Learn more about Blender Conference 2026 at https://conference.blender.org/2026/

snippet.title: A holistic guide to the Hollywood VFX colour pipeline — BCON26
snippet.description:
"A holistic guide to the Hollywood VFX colour pipeline" by Mark Boorer at Blender Conference 2026

Follow along as we find out how to apply the colour science tools of the VFX industry to your own projects. This talk covers processes such as plate linearisation, neutral grading, VFX compositing, CDL grading, and display transforms.
By the end of the talk you should be able to confidently combine and balance footage from different cameras, render with accurate HDRIs, composite correctly, and apply both CDL grades as well as creative display LUTs.
Along the way, we'll be utilising functionality built-in to Blender through OpenColorIO, as well as some other open-source tools.

–

Learn more about Blender Conference 2026 at https://conference.blender.org/2026/

snippet.title: Creative Misuse of the 3D Toolbox — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Creative Misuse of the 3D Toolbox" by Markus Biegholdt, Rob Green at Blender Conference 2026

At Atomhawk, our strategy is built around delivering impactful work, building capability, and evolving how we create, and this 'Studio' talk shows how that translates into real production workflows. The talk explores how Atomhawk implemented Blender not as a traditional 3D package, but as a flexible, idea-driven creative tool within the context of real-world AAA concept pipeline. Offering insight into studio workflows and practical scenarios, it dives into how concept artists use Blender as a design lab and problem-solving environment - prioritising speed, iteration, and artistic intent over technical correctness. By embracing unconventional workflows and non-traditional 3D practices, the emphasis moves beyond software features and toward creative exploration, experimentation, and innovative thinking. Supported by shared assets, custom tools, procedural workflows and automation, Blender becomes a flexible, all-in-one environment for rapid, expressive concept creation. For us, this isn’t just about Blender, it’s about how we make better work, move faster, and keep pushing our creative approach forward.

–

Learn more about Blender Conference 2026 at https://conference.blender.org/2026/

snippet.title: From Final_FINAL_v3 to Making an African Short Film — BCON26
snippet.description:
"From Final_FINAL_v3 to Making an African Short Film" by Taiwo Folu at Blender Conference 2026

There are large studio pipelines and there is the independent freelance artist working solo. Somewhere in between are teams of artists - small studios, remote collaborators, and indie productions - who need something more than a shared drive to create something together.

This talk follows our journey at Eaxum - from pipeline frustration to building Clustta, an open-source version control tool born as a Blender add-on - to actually using it to produce Meji, an African period short film set in the 1900s. 

I'll share how a lean, artist-friendly pipeline enables real shot production in Blender - from layout through animation, lighting, and FX - lowering the barrier to collaboration for independent creators everywhere.

–

Learn more about Blender Conference 2026 at https://conference.blender.org/2026/

snippet.title: Continuing a Lie: Creatures! — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Continuing a Lie: Creatures!" by Omar Hewady at Blender Conference 2026

In this talk, PhotonTown CEO will take you on a journey through the art, technology, and business of creating ultra-hyper-realistic creatures. Drawing from real-world productions, including the creature featured on Zayn Malik's latest album artwork, the animals created for Phish's Sigma Oasis experience at the Las Vegas Sphere...the world's largest screen...the Yeti created for Snippers USA Footwear, and the official lion mascot for the Confederation of African Football (CAF), he will break down the complete workflow from concept to final delivery. Attendees will gain insights into creature design, look development, Blender production pipelines, client collaboration, and the realities of delivering world-class creature work in a professional studio environment.

–

snippet.title: Automotive Design in Blender — BCON26
snippet.description:
"Automotive Design in Blender" by Kim Jern, Rodrigo Candell, Ardalan Farboud at Blender Conference 2026

Automotive design has traditionally relied on NURBS-based workflows, but the modeling team at Zeekr and Lynk & Co Design has gradually adopted Blender as a core tool for both exterior and interior concept development.

In this session, Kim Jern, Rodrigo Candell and Ardalan Farboud will share how Blender fits into their professional automotive design pipeline, what it enables, the challenges they have faced along the way, and where they see opportunities for Blender to go even further in automotive design.

–

snippet.title: CloudRig: Rigging ALL THE THINGS! — BCON26
snippet.description:
"CloudRig: Rigging ALL THE THINGS!" by Demeter Dzadik at Blender Conference 2026

CloudRig is a free rig generation add-on developed by the Blender Studio: https://extensions.blender.org/add-ons/cloudrig/

In this presentation, I will show off some of its latest and lesser known features. I will talk about how you can start using CloudRig if you are already experienced with Rigify, or if you've never tried rigging at all. Hopefully some of the shiny features will spark your curiosity about rigging, which is often seen as a dreaded, finicky part of the 3D animation pipeline. I'd like to show you that it doesn't have to be so scary, in fact it can even be pretty fun, once you have a few basic tools and workflows in your arsenal!

–

Learn more about Blender Conference 2026 at https://conference.blender.org/2026/
